Mashambanzou:The Dawn: New Day, New Opportunities & New Hope for PLWHA 2020-2022

description.narrative: Mashambanzou har sökt 6 miljoner SEK från Sida för att genomföra projektet "The Dawn: New Day, New Opportunity and New Hope for People Living with HIV and AIDS” i Harare under perioden 2020-2022. Insatsen syftar till att förbättra livskvaliteten för människor som lever med - och de som drabbas av - HIV och AIDS genom behandling, vård och stöd för individer, samt genom att ge familjer kunskap och färdigheter för att effektivt hantera chockerna från HIV / AIDS och förbättra lokala samähllens motståndskraft i hanteringen av sjukdomen. Sida kommer också att finansiera installation av solpaneler. Bidraget kommer att vara kärnfinansierat från Sida och det kommer inte att göras andrahandsutbetalningar.

Mashambanzou has applied to Sida for funding of 6 417 500 million SEK to carry out the "The Dawn: New Day, New Opportunities and New Hope for People Living with HIV and AIDS project in Harare, during the period 2020-2022. The intervention aims at improving the quality of life of people living with, and those affected by HIV and AIDS through treatment, care and support of individuals, empowering families with knowledge and skills to effectively respond to the shocks of the HIV/AIDS and improve community resilience in dealing with HIV/AIDS. The contribution will be core funding and there will be no forwarding of funds. Mashambanzou will also receive SEK300 000 for the installation of solar system to improve sustainability of power supply.

Overall Project Objective
To improve the quality of life of people living with, and those affected by HIV and AIDS through treatment, care and support of individuals, families and communities in and around Harare by December 2022.

The End of Project report covers a period of 4 years from 2020 to 2023. Mashambanzou Care Trust (MCT) received a Costed Extension which was covering the gap for 1 year from 2022 to 2023 and this was awarded to allow conclusion of activities that had not been concluded in the 3 years to several reasons including Covid 19 pandemic.
Partnerships
During the period under review, Mashambanzou Care Trust managed to form partnerships with Pharmaceutical & Chemical Distributors (Pvt) Ltd which goes towards MCTs efforts to sustain the Care Unit and Outreach operations with pharmaceutical supplies. Other partnerships forged included a partnership with Zim Meal, a local milling company to donate 300kg of meal mealie monthly as part of the nutrition programme that Mashambanzou Care Unit (MCU) works to provide their patients. This meets the monthly meal-mealie requirement for MCU, Nenyere Day Care Centre (NDCC) and Safe Houses. A partnership with Bakers Inn Zimbabwe resulting in a weekly donation of 60 loaves of bread, which meets the bread requirement for MCU, NDCC and Safe Houses.
Engagement with Line Ministries
MCT engaged the Ministry of Health and Child Care for a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) that would result in the transfer of Care Unit medical staff onto the Government payroll. However, this would require a salary top-up allowance to ensure retention of the health care staff. If this endeavour is successful, a huge relief will be gained as the major and critical component for the project is the nursing care.
Market Gardening/Income Generation
A provision was made for the establishment of the market gardening, an activity which aims to provide 100% vegetable supplies for the Care Unit, NDCC and Safe Houses with surplus being sold to generate more income. This has already been initiated and will look to supporting the Care Unit if managed well for sustainability purposes.
Day Care Centre
Mashambanzou Care Trust managed to enroll 60 pupils for ECD A and ECD B learners without any challenges after covid restrictions had been lifted. The registration and change of name for the Day Care Centre is also work in progress.
Safe Houses
Because Mashambanzou Care Trust uses family centered support, MCT managed to maintain Safe Houses for care for abused children in need, children with parents or guardians who would have been admitted in the Care Unit and vulnerable children with parents or guardians suffering from psychiatric conditions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
